status_note: Still open on main (a4d8e00342d0): [`functions_arithmetic.yaml` L389-L412](https://github.com/substrait-io/substrait/blob/a4d8e00342d0/extensions/functions_arithmetic.yaml#L389-L412) gives `power(i64, i64) -> i64` with `overflow` only and nothing on a negative exponent; `power.test` has positive integer exponents only. No existing issue; [#1001](https://github.com/substrait-io/substrait/pull/1001) (closed) proposed `fp64` results and was declined to keep `int, int -> int`.
summary: `power` of `i64` (`functions_arithmetic.yaml`) returns `i64` and takes only `overflow`. Nothing says what a negative exponent gives, whose result is not an integer: `power(2, -1)` could be `0` (truncated), an error, or a domain error, and the integer implementation has no `on_domain_error`.
repro: `power(2::i64, -1::i64)` and `power(-2::i64, -3::i64)`: the YAML's description, "Take the power with x as the base and y as exponent", defines neither.
Polars 2.1: a negative integer exponent raises (`InvalidOperationError`, fact polars-int-arith); sverify's reference raises (`Issue.negExponent`).
handling: The reference raises on a negative exponent (`Issue.negExponent`, `SubstraitLean/Safety.lean`), an inferred precondition. The core allows raising anywhere (D2), so no option of the catalogue names it; `Profile.substrait` accepts any `on_domain_error` preference for integer `power`, which the YAML does not give it.

Could be expressed as: `on_domain_error: [NULL, ERROR]` on the integer implementations of `power`, as integer `divide` has, with a negative exponent as its domain error, or a sentence in the description.
